Explanation (mechanism): 'Every call to factorial shares one n and one r' is false. Each recursive entry creates a new instance of n and r. The cited passage says so ('a new instance of the object is created each time'), and the claim's own justification says 'every active call has its own'. The text states the opposite of its source and justification.

Mechanism holds: line 7's multiplication needs the value of factorial(n - 1), which is the value its return statement gives back (6.8.6.4p3 passage), and factorial(3)'s n and r stay alive while the call suspends its block (6.2.4p6 passage: calling a function suspends, but does not end, the block). It is true in every program where factorial(3) runs, and the run printed enter factorial(3) then enter factorial(2) before any result.
